title: Dominant reduced parts of finite-generic schemes are alteration objects; etale families
statement: Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Let $\eta$ be its generic point and $K=\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $T$ be a finite type $S$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] whose generic fibre $T_\eta=T\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is finite over $K$ (affine with a finite-dimensional coordinate $K$-algebra), and let $T^{\mathrm{dom}}$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on the union of the irreducible components of $T$ dominating $S$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], [def-pc-reduced-scheme]; this is empty if there are no such components. Then $T^{\mathrm{dom}}$ is finite type over $S$, and every generic point of an irreducible component of $T^{\mathrm{dom}}$ maps to $\eta$ with finite residue field extension. Moreover, if $(v_j:V_j\to T)_j$ is a finite family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism] with every $V_j$ finite type over $S$, then every $V_j$ has finite generic fibre. If in addition the family $(v_j)_j$ is completely decomposed, meaning every $t\in T$ has a lift $z\in V_j$ for some $j$ with $\kappa(t)\to\kappa(z)$ an isomorphism, then the family of base changes $(V_j\times_TT^{\mathrm{dom}}\to T^{\mathrm{dom}})_j$ is completely decomposed. The family may be empty when $T$ is empty.

source.place: Expose III proof of Proposition 3.1(iii), printed p.38: the specialized schemes with finite generic fibre give objects (Y_u)_r, (X'_u)_r, (X_u)_r of alt/S, and the Nisnevich leg restricts to the dominant part; Expose II 1.2.5--1.2.6, printed pp.25--26 ((X_md)_eta finite). Functoriality and the etale identification are the existing lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection] to the finite-type $S$-scheme $T$. Since $S$ is integral it has just the generic point $\eta$ among its component generic points, and the reduced dominant closure in that node is exactly the $T^{\mathrm{dom}}$ of the statement. Its components are precisely the selected components of $T$, so their generic points map to $\eta$. The inclusion $i:T^{\mathrm{dom}}\hookrightarrow T$ is a closed immersion. It is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and composition with $T\to S$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. This proves the finite-type assertion, including the empty dominant part.

source.place: Expose II 1.2.5, printed p.25; Expose III Proposition 3.1(i),(iii), printed pp.37-38; closed-immersion and composition tools are Stacks 01W5 and 01T3

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim], write $T_\eta=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finite-dimensional $K$-algebra through the given structure map. For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset B$, the quotient $B/\mathfrak p$ is a domain spanned over $K$ by the images of any finite spanning set of $B$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] makes $B/\mathfrak p$ a field. Consequently $\mathfrak p$ is maximal and its residue field is $B/\mathfrak p$, finite over $K$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], all irreducible closed subsets of $T_\eta$ are these singleton points, so its topological dimension is at most zero [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], $T_\eta$ is finite type over $K$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian] says that $|T_\eta|$ is discrete (and finite). If $B=0$, its spectrum is empty and the same conclusions hold without choosing a prime.

source.place: Expose II proof of 1.2.6, printed p.25 (finite generic fibre); finite algebra calculation as in Stacks 01WH, 00ES (lemma-irreducible), and 00KH (lemma-Noetherian-dimension-0)

proof.text: Let $\xi$ be a component generic point of $T^{\mathrm{dom}}$ and $t=i(\xi)$. Step 1 gives $t\mapsto\eta$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] there is a point $w$ of $T_\eta$ above $t$: the relevant tensor ring is $\kappa(t)\otimes_K K\simeq\kappa(t)$ with prime zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field], $\kappa(w)\simeq\kappa(t)$ compatibly with $K$. Step 2 therefore makes $\kappa(t)/K$ finite. The closed immersion $i$ induces an isomorphism $\kappa(t)\simeq\kappa(\xi)$: locally it is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and at a corresponding prime $\mathfrak q\supset I$ both residues are $\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Thus $\kappa(\xi)/K$ is finite through the actual structure map. If $T^{\mathrm{dom}}$ is empty there are no such $\xi$.

source.place: Expose III Proposition 3.1(i),(iii), printed pp.37-38 (membership in alt/S); Stacks 01JT (lemma-points-fibre-product) and 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion)

proof.text: Fix $j$ and put $W=(V_j)_\eta$. It is finite type over $K$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], using the assumed finite type of $V_j\to S$. Associativity of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies the induced map $a:W\to T_\eta$ with the base change of $v_j$. It is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], hence unramified and locally of finite type by [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-unramified-morphism]. For $w\in W$ with image $t\in T_\eta$, [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-fibre-point-isolated] says $w$ is isolated in $a^{-1}(t)$, using the fibre/subspace identification of [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Step 2 makes $\{t\}$ open in $T_\eta$, so $a^{-1}(t)$ is open in $W$. A singleton open in that open subspace is open in $W$. This holds for every $w$, hence $W$ is discrete. No separation assumption on $V_j$ or $v_j$ is used.

source.place: Expose III proof of Proposition 3.1(iii), printed p.38, the Nisnevich leg; Stacks 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type), 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale), 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), topological part

proof.text: In a discrete space any subset containing two distinct points is the union of two proper closed subsets (a singleton and its complement within the subset), so every nonempty irreducible closed subset is a singleton. Thus Step 4 gives $\dim W\le0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The equality in [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] identifies this topological dimension with the local-ring dimension used in [lem-pc-algebraic-dim-zero-affine-finite]. Apply that lemma to the finite-type $K$-scheme $W$: its structure morphism is finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim] this also means it is affine with finite-dimensional coordinate $K$-algebra, as required by the statement's meaning of finite generic fibre. For empty $W$ the affine coordinate ring is the zero ring, of dimension zero as a $K$-vector space; the structural map is finite directly from [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. This argument applies separately to every $j$; finiteness of the index set is not needed here.

Assume the family is completely decomposed. Fix $t'\in T^{\mathrm{dom}}$, put $t=i(t')$, and choose $j,z$ over $t$ for which $\alpha:\kappa(t)\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism. Write $\beta:\kappa(t)\to\kappa(t')$ for the map induced by $i$. The tensor ring $\kappa(z)\otimes_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(t')$ is isomorphic to $\kappa(t')$ by $a\otimes b\mapsto\beta(\alpha^{-1}(a))b$, with inverse $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. Its zero prime gives a point $z'$ in $V_j\times_T T^{\mathrm{dom}}$ above $(z,t')$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field] the induced map $\kappa(t')\to\kappa(z')$ is the displayed isomorphism, since the tensor ring is already a field. This proves the required completely decomposed property at every $t'$. These maps remain etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. If $T$ is empty then $T^{\mathrm{dom}}$ is empty and the assertion is vacuous, even for the empty family.

The statement is byte-identical to the live base. The 4 added stmt_deps (generic point, scheme fibre, field extension, reduced induced subscheme) are all used in the statement, and no stmt_dep was dropped. The delivery has no new nodes and no SGA, and the dependency closure (130 nodes) contains no cycle. Step 1: the coreflection X_md equals T^dom for integral S; finite type via closed-immersion-proper (a) and composition. Step 2: B/p is a field (finite-dimensional domain), every prime is maximal, dim<=0 via 00ES, and 00KH-node discreteness applies with finite type. Step 3: 01JT gives the point plus the residue-field iso through the tensor field kappa(t)(x)_K K, and a closed immersion preserves residue fields. Step 4: (V_j)_eta is finite type from the V_j->S hypothesis; the base change is etale (02GO); 02G7 makes w isolated in the fibre, which is open because {t} is open, so W is discrete with no separatedness used. Step 5: the 04MU bridge from topological to local-ring dimension feeds 06LH (non-proper); the empty case is handled. Step 6: the tensor kappa(z)(x)_{kappa(t)}kappa(t') is isomorphic to kappa(t') via beta∘alpha^{-1}, so the zero prime gives a residue-preserving lift and the family stays completely decomposed. Tested cases: T empty; Spec k[e]/e^2 over k; Spec Z ⊔ Spec F_p over Z; etale V over Spec Z. No duplicates: generic-fibre-finiteness-criterion is the converse, and alteration-cover-calculus and etale-covering-base-change lack the residue clause. Accepted the 12 generic Stacks tool_uses. Advisory only: generic point and field extension are not bracketed inline in the statement, but stmt_deps carry them.
